name: PHD (Proxy + Human Demonstration) Analysis
description: A sophisticated zero-shot detection framework that evaluates text by utilizing a 'Proxy' language model combined with 'Human Demonstration' baselines. Because commercial AI models (like GPT-4 or Claude 3) are 'black boxes' that don't reveal their internal token probabilities, this method uses a smaller, accessible proxy model to estimate how a machine likely generated the text, and contrasts those estimations against verified human writing patterns.
algorithm: Proxy-Estimated Probability Curvature and Demonstration Alignment
mechanism: The algorithm employs an accessible, open-weights Proxy Model (like Llama-3 or Mistral) to analyze the target text. The Proxy Model reads the text and calculates the probability of each word having been generated sequentially. Simultaneously, the system compares these proxy-derived probabilities against a robust dataset of 'Human Demonstrations'—verified human writing samples featuring high semantic variance, colloquial nuances, and uneven predictabilities. If the text's probability distribution aligns neatly with the Proxy Model's optimized generation path (showing a smooth, high-probability 'machine curve'), the text is classified as AI-generated. If the text deviates wildly from the proxy model's predictions and aligns closer to the chaotic variance of the human demonstration dataset, it is classified as human. This method bypasses the need for direct access to the original AI's source code by assuming all advanced language models share fundamentally similar mathematical architectures and gradient preferences.
useCase: Essential for detecting texts generated by closed-source, proprietary 'black-box' models (like OpenAI's GPT-4o or Google's Gemini) where traditional, precise perplexity analysis is impossible because the model's internal data is hidden from the public.
strengths:
• Detector-agnostic and highly resilient: It does not need to be trained on the specific AI model that generated the text.
• Highly effective against commercial, closed-source models by using open-source proxies.
• Reduces false positives by anchoring its judgment strictly against real human demonstration data rather than pure statistical theory.
limitations:
• Computationally expensive compared to simple statistical metrics like n-gram analysis, as it requires running the text through a live neural network (the proxy model).
• If an open-source proxy model is vastly inferior to the black-box model that generated the text, the predictability correlation may temporarily break down.
• Can struggle with highly technical documents where human writing naturally mirrors the highly structured, predictable nature of AI.
parameters:
Analysis: Proxy LLM Token Probability Estimation
Metric: Proxy-Curve Alignment vs. Human Demonstration Baseline
Output: 0-100 PHD (Proxy-Predicted Artificiality) Score
accuracy: High — 85-95% accuracy in black-box scenarios. Provides one of the most robust zero-shot detection mechanisms currently available for modern, proprietary AI models.

references.title: Bao, J. et al. (2024). POGER: Proxy-Guided Efficient Re-sampling for Black-box AI-Generated Text Detection. IJCAI.
Mitchell, E. et al. (2023). DetectGPT: Zero-Shot Machine-Generated Text Detection using Probability Curvature. ICML.
